verifiedScope.proxy: Selected fantasy-fiction first-publication window, from Phantastes to Lilith, used as a publishing proxy rather than a full-career span or a claim of uninterrupted writing. Phantastes and Lilith use first English-language book years; the other four markers date the opening year of serialization, not completion or later book editions. The Portent began in The Cornhill Magazine in 1860; At the Back of the North Wind began in Good Words for the Young in 1868; The Princess and the Goblin began there in 1870; The Princess and Curdie was serialized in 1877. Bibliographies catalogue their book editions under 1864, 1871, 1872 and 1883 respectively; imprint years should not be confused with first serial appearances. Lilith’s first draft was completed in 1890, before its 1895 publication. Poetry, sermons, translations, realistic fiction, other tales, reissues and posthumous releases are outside this selection; later works do not extend this scoped bar.
